document.abstract: An efficient method for regulating the speed of a high-speed motion-picture camera is described. A reluctance pickup is placed near the sprocket teeth of the drive spindle on a Fastax camera. Each time that a sprocket tooth passes the pickup, a voltage pulse is generated. The amount of time between pulses is measured and compared with the desired amount of time. An error signal is derived that controls the conduction angle for a pair of thyratrons. The thyratrons control the power into the camera motors and hence the camera speed. This sampled data feedback loop allows one to control the picture rate of the camera with a high degree of precision. When power is applied, the camera accelerates rapidly to the preselected speed and maintains this speed until power is removed. This method is not only useful at high picture-taking rates but is also effective at speeds much lower than are normally possible with a high-speed camera. This activity has support from the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force.
